claims.citation: New York Herald, 17 July 1866, p. 8, col. 5
claims.verbatim:
Steamship Marathon (Br), Edmonson, Liverpool July 3,
via Queenstown 4th, with mdse and 423 passengers, to E
Cunard. July 3, 4:30 PM, off Bell Buoy, passed a large ship,
supposed the ship Neptune, going into Liverpool; 4th, steam
ship Helvetia, off Queenstown harbor; 10:30 PM, exchanged
signals with steamship Great Eastern, 10 miles east of Fast-
net; 5th, lat 51 22, lon 12 15, steamship Scotia, hence for
Liverpool; 13th, lat 42 40, lon 55 37, steamship Java (or Tripo-
li), bound E; 16 miles east of Cape Race, passed three ice-
bergs. Experienced strong westerly winds most of the pas-
sage.

claims.claim: Spoken / sighted in lat. 43 40, long. 55 37 (13th inst.)
claims.verbatim:
Steamship Marathon (Br), Edmonson, Liverpool, July 3, and
Queenstown the 4th, with mdse. and 423 pass. to E. Cunard. July 3,
at 4:30 p. m., off Bell Buoy passed a large ship, supposed to be the
American ship Neptune, going into Liverpool; July 4, steamship Hel-
vetia, off Queenstown harbor; July 4, at 10:30 p. m., exchanged sig-
nals with steamship Great Eastern, 10 miles SE of Fastnet; July 5,
in lat. 51 22, long. 12 15, steamship Scotia, bound E., 13th inst., in lat.
43 40, long. 55 37, steamship[?] Java or Tripoli, bound E., 16 miles E of [cut]
